requirement:
The harness checks the submission count in a complete model response before
checking submission arguments. An otherwise valid submission while any search
page is open returns a tool error listing every outstanding `search_id` and
instructing the agent to call `finish_search` before resubmitting. The request
stays open and retains its submission reminder. Once all delivered searches
are accounted for under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior`,
exactly one `submit_result` call whose arguments are an object containing only
the `result` field supplies that field's value for decoding and vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. Acceptance ends the
conversation. Other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped.
Assistant prose remains conversation text.
rationale: Add a test (for example next to `count_is_checked_before_arguments_and_one_reminder_allows_recovery` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs`) in which one model response contains exactly one valid `submit_result` with `{"result":...}`, with no search open, plus another tool call such as `read_node`. Assert that the answer is accepted and the conversation ends, with no further provider request. Also assert that the other call was not executed: no graph read, no recorded dependency, and no `read_node` entry in the tool usage. Mark the test with `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. — The text says that other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped. That covers an accepted submission, not only a rejected one. The marked tests only show skipping in rejection cases. In `count_is_checked_before_arguments_and_one_reminder_allows_recovery`, a duplicate-count response skips `read_node`. In `outstanding_search_preserves_the_prior_missing_submission_reminder`, a submission with an open search skips `read_node`. In `configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions` and `supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport`, every accepted `submit_result` is the only call in its response. An implementation that skips sibling calls only when it rejects, but runs them when it accepts, would pass all of these tests. That behavior breaks the clause, because it would record reads and dependencies, and could run tools, after the answer is accepted.

text: :::{req} submission.acceptance
The harness checks the submission count in a complete model response before
checking submission arguments. An otherwise valid submission while any search
page is open returns a tool error listing every outstanding `search_id` and
instructing the agent to call `finish_search` before resubmitting. The request
stays open and retains its submission reminder. Once all delivered searches
are accounted for under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior`,
exactly one `submit_result` call whose arguments are an object containing only
the `result` field supplies that field's value for decoding and vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. Acceptance ends the
conversation. Other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped.
Assistant prose remains conversation text.
:::{req} finish_search.behavior
Each text or structural search page delivered to the agent opens a session-local
`search_id` for accounting, even when there are no matches. Each match has a
short string `tag` unique within the page. Each new page receives a fresh UUID. The agent may fetch further pages
while earlier pages are open. Replaying a page preserves its ID, tags, and
completion state. Failed searches and undelivered pages create no obligation.
Before the harness accepts a submission, the agent MUST call `finish_search`
for every open page. `used` lists the tags of excerpts the agent relied on
directly and may be empty. A valid call closes the page and returns its ID and
`finished: true`. A later call for the same page can select additional tags.

The tool accepts exactly `search_id` and `used`. An invalid call, including an unknown ID or tag, returns a correctable tool error and preserves the page's completion state. A submission with open pages returns a tool error listing every outstanding UUID so the agent can close them and resubmit in the same conversation.
:::{req} vet_answer
Each call to `Ask::vet_answer` appends an independent `FnMut` callback to this
request in either builder phase.
For each decoded submission, the harness invokes the callbacks in registration
order with the same `&R`, stopping at the first `Err`. Each callback retains
its state across submissions in the same conversation.
If any callback returns `Err(error)`, the harness MUST stop running callbacks
and end the conversation immediately, even if an earlier callback requested a
correction. Awaiting the `Ask` MUST return
`Err(ValidationError::Graph(error))` carrying the original `D::Error`.

output.rationale:
`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance` states only observable harness behavior. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface that the implementation must use.

- **Ordering of checks:** the submission count is checked before the arguments. A harness that validated differently internally would still behave the same way, as long as the visible outcome is the same.
- **Open search pages:** an otherwise valid submission while any page is open returns a tool error that lists every outstanding `search_id` and tells the agent to call `finish_search`. The request stays open and keeps its reminder. All of this is visible in the tool result and the conversation state.
- **Accepted submission:** exactly one `submit_result` call, with an object containing only `result`, supplies the value that is decoded and vetted. Acceptance ends the conversation. Other tool calls in the same response are skipped, and assistant prose stays conversation text. These are all outcomes of the protocol.
- **Cited requirements:** `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior` and `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer` are only cited. They provide context, and any structural obligations they carry belong to their own assessments.

Every clause could be met by a different internal design with identical observable results. No implementation roots are needed, and none were supplied.
